questions.text: The line notes of the treble clef, from bottom to top, spell...
The space notes of the treble clef, from bottom to top, spell...
How long does one eighth note last?
The dynamic symbol f tells you to play...
The note that sits on a ledger line just below the treble staff is...
In solfege, the syllable do matches which note of the C major scale?

Now that you finished Module 19, explain in a short paragraph (3 to 5 sentences): how do you read a line of music? Mention how you name the notes, how you find each note value, and how you read the dynamics.
How sure do you feel about reading the notes, note values, and dynamics on a treble-clef staff?
Which part of reading music felt hardest this week (note names, note values, dynamics, or the ledger-line note)? What helped you?
I can name the line notes (EGBDF) and the space notes (FACE).
I can read a short line in solfege (do to la).
Reading music takes perseverance: you keep practicing even when it is tricky. Tell about a moment this week when you stuck with a hard note or rhythm until you got it.
A saying or word that helps you remember something, like a fruit word for a rhythm, is called a...
How many eighth notes fit in one beat?
How long does a dotted half note last?
How long does a dotted quarter note last?
Copying back a rhythm you hear is called...
Saying a fruit word like "ap-ple" at a steady speed can help you remember an eighth-note pair.
Now that you finished Module 20: in your own words, what is a mnemonic, and how can it help you read rhythm?
How sure do you feel about reading eighth-note pairs and dotted notes?
Which fruit-word mnemonic will you use to remember a rhythm, and which note does it stand for?
I can tell how long a dotted half note and a dotted quarter note last.
I recorded myself practicing a rhythm pattern.

Reading rhythm takes perseverance, which means sticking with something even when it feels tricky. Write 3 to 5 sentences about a rhythm or note value that was hard at first this week, what you did to keep practicing, and how it felt once it started to click.
What does K-Pop stand for?
K-Pop is a kind of popular music that comes from which country?
Which part of a song repeats with the same words and tune each time it comes around?
The short, super-catchy part of a song you cannot stop singing is called the...
On the treble-clef staff, the four spaces (from bottom to top) spell which word?
The carefully planned dancing that goes with a K-Pop song is called...
Now that you finished Module 21: what is K-Pop, and where does it come from? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about naming the verse, chorus, and hook in a song's form?
What was your favorite part of this week: learning about K-Pop, the reading game, or recording the rhythm? Tell why.
I can name the verse, chorus, and hook of a song.
I can read notes on the treble-clef staff.

This week you listened to music from another country. Showing courtesy means treating something from another culture with respect and curiosity. In two or three sentences, tell what you found interesting or beautiful about K-Pop, and how listening with courtesy helped you enjoy music sung in another language.
What does a conductor do?

answers.text: Plays the loudest instrument in the group
Leads the group and keeps everyone on a steady beat
Writes the words to the song
Tunes all the instruments before the concert

questions.text: The thin stick that some conductors hold to make the beat easy to see is called a...
The downbeat is beat 1 of the measure. Which way does the downbeat always go?
The last beat of a measure, when the hand rises back up to get ready for the next beat 1, is called the...
Which conducting pattern traces a triangle shape with your hand: down, out, up?
In the 2/4 conducting pattern, which way does your hand move on beat 1, and which way on beat 2?
Now that you finished Module 22: in your own words, what does a conductor do?
How sure do you feel about conducting the 2/4, 3/4, and 4/4 patterns and keeping a steady beat?
Which conducting pattern felt easiest to you: 2/4, 3/4, or 4/4? Which one felt the trickiest, and why?
I can tell what the downbeat and the upbeat are.
I conducted a rhythmic challenge and recorded it.

Keeping a steady beat and leading yourself or a group takes self-government: staying calm and in control of your own pulse so others can follow you. Write three to five sentences about a time you had to stay in control and keep going steadily, even when it was hard to hold the pace. How did conducting this week help you practice self-government?
The lines of the treble clef staff, from bottom to top, are E, G, B, D, and...
The four spaces of the treble clef spell what word?
A dotted half note lasts how many beats?
Two eighth notes together last the same as...
Many K-Pop songs repeat a catchy section called the...
In every conducting pattern, beat 1 always moves in which direction?
Which conducting pattern makes the shape of a triangle (down, out, up)?
While you conduct, what should your hand do when you reach a long note like a half note?

answers.text: stop and wait until the note ends
keep moving steadily through the beats

questions.text: Now that you finished Module 23: in your own words, what is a conducting pattern, and what is it for?
How sure do you feel about drawing the 2/4, 3/4, and 4/4 conducting patterns?
Which pattern, 2/4, 3/4, or 4/4, was the trickiest for you to keep steady while reading, and what made it tricky?
I can draw the 2/4, 3/4, and 4/4 conducting patterns.
I conducted a steady pattern while I read through a practice exercise.

Conducting takes self-government: you have to keep your own hand steady and your own beat even when no one is watching. Tell about a moment this week when you had to stay disciplined and keep your beat going, even when it was hard.
Which four instruments make up the string family of the orchestra?

answers.text: Violin, viola, cello, and double bass

questions.text: Which string instrument is the biggest and lowest?
Put the strings in order from highest to lowest.
Playing a string instrument by drawing a bow across the strings is called...
What does pizzicato mean?

answers.text: Plucking the strings with a finger

questions.text: Antonio Vivaldi is famous for writing which work?
Now that you finished Module 24: name the four instruments of the string family in order from highest to lowest. Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about the string family and the difference between bowing (arco) and plucking (pizzicato)?
What was your favorite part of learning about the strings or Vivaldi this week?
I can name the violin, viola, cello, and double bass and put them in order high to low.
I made my Strings Family Video with all three parts.

Making a video with three parts takes responsibility: you have to plan it, finish each part, and turn it in on time. Tell how you took responsibility for your work this week, or what you would do to stay organized next time.
Which string instrument is the smallest and makes the highest sound?
Compared with the violin, the viola is...

answers.text: slightly larger, and sounds darker and lower

questions.text: In the orchestra, which instrument most often plays the melody, the tune you can hum?
What is the sticky stuff a player rubs on the bow so it grips the strings?
The space notes of the treble clef, from bottom to top, spell what word?
The bright, high sound of the violin is like the soprano voice, and the warmer, lower viola is like the alto voice.
Now that you finished Module 25: How are the violin and the viola alike, and how are they different? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about telling the violin and the viola apart, and reading the treble clef?
Is anything still fuzzy or tricky about the violin, the viola, or reading the lines and spaces? Tell us what, so we can help.
I can tell the violin and the viola apart by their size and sound.
I can read treble-clef lines and spaces with different note values.

Reading notes and recording yourself can be hard at first, and it takes perseverance to keep going and try again until it sounds right. Tell about one part of this week's video that you had to practice or try more than once before you got it.
How do you play the cello?

answers.text: Sitting down, with the instrument between the knees

questions.text: Which string instrument is the largest and plays the lowest pitch?
Plucking a string with your fingers instead of using the bow is called...
What is another name for the cello?
In solfege, which note does the syllable la match?
The deep, low sound of the double bass gives the orchestra a strong foundation.
Now that you finished Module 26: Which string instrument is the largest and plays the lowest pitch, and why does the orchestra need it? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about telling the cello and the double bass apart, and reading the treble clef?
Is anything still fuzzy or tricky about the cello, the double bass, or reading and singing the notes? Tell us what, so we can help.
I can describe the cello and the double bass and tell them apart.
I can read treble-clef notes and sing the solfege ladder up to la.

Getting faster and more accurate at reading music takes perseverance, which means sticking with something even when it is hard. Tell about one part of your reading or recording this week that you kept practicing until it got better.
How is the flute played?

answers.text: Held sideways and blown across a hole

questions.text: What gives the oboe its thin, reedy sound?
Which family do the flute and the oboe belong to?
In Peter and the Wolf, which instrument plays the bird?
A leap of a third...

answers.text: moves to the very next note

questions.text: Prokofiev gave each character in Peter and the Wolf its own instrument.
Now that you finished Module 27: How can instruments tell a story? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about telling the flute and the oboe apart, and reading a leap of a third?
Is anything still fuzzy or tricky about the woodwinds, Prokofiev, or thirds? Tell us what, so we can help.
I can tell the flute and the oboe apart by how they are played and how they sound.
I can read a leap of a third on the staff.

The Quarter 3 Live VR Experience brings the whole class together. Showing courtesy means taking turns, listening to others, and being kind in the shared space. Tell about one way you showed courtesy to a classmate or your teacher during the live VR session.
What kind of reed does the clarinet use?
Which woodwind is the lowest of all?
The clarinet is sometimes nicknamed the...
An interval is...
C up to D, with no note skipped, is a...
C up to E, which skips one note, is a...
Now that you finished Module 28: What is an interval, and how can you tell a second from a third? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about telling the clarinet and the bassoon apart, and telling a second from a third?
Is anything still fuzzy or tricky about the clarinet, the bassoon, or intervals? Tell us what, so we can help.
I can describe the clarinet and the bassoon and tell their reeds apart.
I can tell a second apart from a third on the staff.

Learning to read intervals takes perseverance, which means sticking with something even when it feels hard at first. Tell about one part of this week's work that took you more than one try, and how you kept going until you understood it.
How does a brass player make sound?

answers.text: By buzzing the lips into a mouthpiece
By hitting it with a stick

questions.text: Which brass instrument is the smallest and plays the highest?
The three buttons a trumpet player presses to change notes are called...
What does a sharp do to a note?
A flat does what to a note?
A natural sign tells the player to...

answers.text: put the note back to its plain pitch

questions.text: Now that you finished Module 29: how does a brass player make sound, and what do the sharp, flat, and natural signs do? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about the trumpet and the three accidentals (sharp, flat, natural)?
Is anything still fuzzy or tricky about the brass family, the trumpet, or the accidentals? Tell us what, so we can help.
I can explain how a brass player makes sound and name the trumpet's valves.
I can tell what the sharp, flat, and natural signs do to a note.

Drawing the three signs and reading a line with accidentals can be tricky at first. Showing perseverance means you keep trying even when something is hard, instead of giving up. Tell about one part of this week that took perseverance, and how you kept going.
Which family does the French horn belong to?
What helps give the French horn its warm, mellow sound?
What does a sharp (#) do to a note?
How do we write B-flat in our keyboard format?
What does a natural sign do?

answers.text: Cancels a sharp or flat and returns a note to its plain pitch
Raises a note two whole steps

questions.text: The French horn is often called one of the most difficult brass instruments to play.
Now that you finished Module 30: What makes the French horn special, and how do accidentals change a note? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about describing the French horn and labeling notes with accidentals (A#, Bb, Cn)?
Is anything still fuzzy or tricky about the French horn, sharps, flats, or naturals? Tell us what, so we can help.
I can describe the French horn and what gives it its warm, mellow sound.
I can label a note as a sharp, flat, or natural using the format A#, Bb, or Cn.

The French horn is often called the most difficult brass instrument to play, and labeling accidentals takes careful practice. Showing perseverance means sticking with something hard and not giving up. Tell about one part of music this week that took perseverance for you, and how you kept going.
How does a trombone change its notes?

answers.text: It moves a slide in and out

questions.text: A trombone slide has how many positions?
What does a sharp do to a note?
Which accidental cancels a sharp or a flat and returns the note to normal?
The long sliding sound a trombone can make is called a...
Most trombones are tenor trombones, which play in a middle-to-low range.
Now that you finished Module 31: how does a trombone change its notes? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about reading sharps, flats, and naturals out loud?
What was your favorite part of learning about the trombone this week?
I can describe the trombone and explain that it uses a slide instead of valves.
I recorded myself reading a line of notes with accidentals.

Reading notes out loud, especially ones with accidentals, takes perseverance. That means you keep trying even when it feels hard. Tell about a time this week when you had to read your line again to get it right. How did it feel to keep going?
The clarinet makes its sound with what kind of reed?
The distance between two notes is called an...
The trumpet is a brass instrument that is...
A sharp sign tells a musician to play a note...
The French horn is a brass instrument known for its long tubing coiled into a...
The trombone changes its notes by moving a long...
Which brass instrument is the largest and plays the lowest notes?
A major interval sounds happy and bright. A minor interval sounds...
Now that you finished Module 32: How can your ear tell a happy major interval from a sad minor one? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about telling a major interval from a minor interval by ear?
Is anything still fuzzy or tricky about the tuba or about major and minor intervals? Tell us what, so we can help.
I can describe the tuba as the largest and lowest brass instrument.
I can sing a two-note interval using the syllable "LA."

Ear training is hard at first, and it gets better only when you keep practicing. Showing perseverance means you keep trying even when something feels tricky. Tell about one moment this week when you had to keep singing or listening again before you could hear the difference between major and minor.
How do you play a percussion instrument?

answers.text: By striking, shaking, or scraping it

questions.text: Which of these is a PITCHED percussion instrument?
Which of these is an UNPITCHED percussion instrument?
What is the pattern of steps in a major scale?

answers.text: Half, half, whole, half, half, half, whole
Whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half
Whole, whole, whole, whole, whole, whole, whole
Half, whole, half, whole, half, whole, half

questions.text: In the C major scale, the half steps fall between...

answers.text: E and F, and between B and C

questions.text: In solfege, the syllable do matches which note of the C major scale?
Now that you finished Module 33: what is the difference between pitched and unpitched percussion? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about the major-scale pattern (whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half)?
Which percussion instrument was your favorite this week, and why?
I can tell pitched percussion from unpitched percussion.
I sang or played a major scale and recorded it.

Singing a whole scale and keeping each pitch steady takes perseverance, which means sticking with something even when it is hard. Tell about a moment this week when you kept practicing the scale until it got better.
How many beats does a whole note last in 4/4 time?
In music, a rest tells you to...

answers.text: be silent for a number of beats
play as loud as you can

questions.text: What does the top number of a time signature tell you?

answers.text: How many beats are in each measure

questions.text: The space notes of the treble clef, from bottom to top, spell what word?
A short extra line used for a note that is too high or too low to fit on the five staff lines is called a...
On the solfege ladder, which syllable do you sing for the note C?
Now that you finished Module 34: name one rhythm or notation topic you reviewed this week (for example, note values, time signatures, rests, treble clef, ledger lines, note names, or solfege).
How sure do you feel about reading rhythm and notes on the treble clef?
Which topic from this week do you still want to practice more before the year ends?
I can name the note values and tell how many beats each one lasts.
I can name notes on the treble clef and sing them in solfege.
Reviewing and sticking with the parts that feel tricky takes perseverance. Tell about a music topic you kept working on this week even when it was hard, and how it felt to keep going.
Which of these is a parameter of music?
Dynamics in music tell us...

answers.text: How fast or slow it is
How loud or soft it is
How high or low it is

questions.text: On the treble clef, the line notes from bottom to top are...
Which composer kept writing music even after he became deaf?
Louis Armstrong is famous as a...
Match each form word to what it means.

answers.right: the part that repeats with the same words
part A, then part B, then part A returns
one part, then a different second part

questions.text: Now that you finished Module 35: name one thing you reviewed this week that you feel sure about. Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about naming the form of a song (AB, ABA, verse and chorus)?
Which composer or musician from this year (Mozart, Beethoven, Louis Armstrong, or Dave Brubeck) was your favorite, and why?
I can name the parameters of music and what expression symbols do.
I can identify the form of a song (AB, ABA, or verse and chorus).

Reviewing your own work and your Music Journal takes responsibility. Tell about one way you took responsibility for your learning this week (for example, going back to fix something you forgot or practicing on your own).
Which instrument belongs to the string family?
You make sound on a brass instrument by...

answers.text: Buzzing your lips into a mouthpiece

questions.text: What does a flat do to a note?
In solfege, which syllable matches the note A?
What does a conductor do?

answers.text: Keeps the beat and leads the musicians

questions.text: Which composer kept writing music even after he became deaf?
Now that you finished Module 36: name the four instrument families in your own words.
How sure do you feel about the big review topics (the instrument families, accidentals, conducting, and composers)?
Which review topic was your favorite to look back on this week, and why?
I can name the four instrument families and an instrument in each.
I can read the solfege syllables do, re, mi, fa, sol, la.

You have nearly finished a whole year of music. Finishing strong takes perseverance. Tell about a time this year when you kept practicing or reviewing even when it was hard, and how it helped you grow.
Think back to the very beginning of the year. What is something about music you understand now that you did not understand back then?
How do you feel as a music scholar now?
What was your favorite unit or topic we studied this year? (An instrument family, a composer, reading music, a song, a music word, anything!) Tell why you liked it.
I can name instruments from the four families (strings, woodwinds, brass, percussion).
I can read notes on the treble clef staff.
I can hear and name feelings in music using dynamics and tempo (loud/soft, fast/slow).
Name one music skill you grew in this year. What can you do now that was hard for you at the start?
You worked hard all year long, and finishing the whole year takes perseverance. What are you most proud of learning in music this year?
Set one music goal for next year. What is something you want to learn, get better at, or try?
Leave a short message about your year in music class. This is your final check-in for the year. Have a wonderful summer, music scholar!
